jurisdiction.name: Generic city checklist (used when a city is not yet in the catalog)
jurisdiction.notes: Typical local permits every US city or county issues for food and beverage businesses. Names, agencies, fees and timelines vary; treat these as a checklist to confirm with the local permit center.

permits.name: City / county business license or tax registration
permits.issuing_agency: City clerk, finance department or county tax collector
permits.notes: Nearly every municipality requires a general business license or business tax certificate before opening; some counties also require one for unincorporated areas.

permits.name: Zoning clearance / certificate of occupancy for the use
permits.notes: Confirm the address allows a restaurant/bar use before signing the lease. Bars, late-night hours, live entertainment and outdoor seating frequently require a conditional or special use permit with a public hearing (3–9 months).
permits.stall_risk: A conditional use hearing is usually the longest item in the plan; start it before build-out.

permits.name: Building permit (tenant improvements / change of occupancy)
permits.notes: Kitchen build-outs, hoods, restrooms, accessibility upgrades and any change of occupancy require stamped plans and inspections; electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are usually separate.

permits.name: Health department plan review (new food facility)
permits.issuing_agency: County or city environmental health department
permits.notes: Floor plans, equipment schedules and menu are reviewed before construction; approval is a prerequisite for the operating permit inspection.

permits.name: Food service establishment permit (health permit)
permits.issuing_agency: County or city environmental health department
permits.notes: Issued after a pre-opening inspection; required before serving the public. Annual renewal with routine inspections.

permits.name: Fire department inspection / assembly occupancy permit
permits.notes: Occupant load posting, hood suppression system test, extinguishers and egress are checked before the certificate of occupancy is released.

permits.name: Grease interceptor / FOG discharge permit
permits.notes: Most sewer utilities require food service establishments to install and maintain a grease interceptor and keep pumping logs.

permits.name: Sign permit
permits.notes: Exterior and illuminated signs almost always need a permit; historic districts add design review.

permits.name: Entertainment / amplified sound / cabaret permit
permits.issuing_agency: City clerk, police department or dedicated entertainment commission
permits.notes: Live music, DJs, dancing and amplified outdoor sound typically need a separate permit with neighbor notice and sometimes a hearing.

permits.name: Sidewalk cafe / outdoor dining permit
permits.notes: Seating in the public right-of-way needs a revocable permit, an ADA clear path, and liability insurance naming the city.

permits.name: Hotel / lodging tax registration and lodging license
permits.notes: Register to collect the local transient occupancy / hotel tax; many cities also issue a lodging or hotel license tied to fire and housing inspections.

permits.name: Mobile food vending permit
permits.issuing_agency: City and county health department / public works
permits.notes: Trucks and carts need a health permit for the vehicle, a commissary agreement, and a vending or location permit from the city.
